landscape: Research on armed conflict rests on two data traditions. The first produces annual lists of conflicts and wars: the UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset (from 1946), the Correlates of War intra-state and non-state wars, and lists built for specific studies (Fearon-Laitin, Sambanis, PITF, MEPV). The second records events: UCDP's Georeferenced Event Dataset and ACLED code individual violent events with locations, while machine-coded event data (GDELT, ICEWS and its successor POLECAT, Cline Center Phoenix) process news reports at scale. UCDP has become the hub of the field, with linked datasets on actors, external support, termination, peace agreements, one-sided violence and non-state conflict.

Around this core sit datasets on specific forms of violence and on conflict processes: terrorism (the Global Terrorism Database, RAND, ITERATE, suicide attacks), coups (Powell-Thyne, the Cline Center, Colpus), pro-government militias, mass killing and atrocities (PITF, Targeted Mass Killing) and electoral violence (ECAV, DECO). Further datasets record armed-group attributes (Non-State Actor data, FORGE, BAAD), peace agreements (UCDP, PA-X, Peace Accords Matrix), mediation and ceasefires; the Ethnic Power Relations family links ethnic politics to conflict.

The domain has 154 CONF rows plus GeoEPR (catalogued under GEO). Many specialised datasets are single releases tied to one article and are now frozen. Important series have also ended or changed access: the Global Terrorism Database stopped at 2020, ICEWS ended in 2023, and ACLED now requires registration and limits redistribution. Several sites block automated access and some old project domains now host unrelated content, so the catalog links only to verified official pages.

core.text: The UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset (version 26.1) lists all armed conflicts from 1946 to 2025 between a government and another government or an organized opposition group that cause at least 25 battle-related deaths in a year. It records intensity, type and parties. It is widely used as a country-year and conflict-year source and anchors the linked UCDP datasets. Its low death threshold captures minor conflicts that war lists omit, so results can differ from studies using war-level thresholds.

The UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset records individual events of organized violence (state-based, non-state and one-sided) with dates, locations and low, best and high fatality estimates, globally from 1989 to 2025. It is a common source for subnational analyses of violence and supports grid-level work through PRIO-GRID. Inclusion requires a fatal event in a UCDP-defined conflict, so non-fatal violence is excluded.

The Armed Conflict Location & Event Data project codes political violence and demonstrations worldwide, with weekly updates and coverage that starts in 1997 for Africa and later for other regions. It records non-fatal as well as fatal events and many actor types, which makes it suited to studying protest, riots and violence against civilians. Access requires registration under a licence that restricts redistribution, and coverage start years differ across regions.

The Global Terrorism Database records more than 200,000 terrorist attacks worldwide from 1970 to 2020, with attack type, target, weapon, perpetrator and casualties, including domestic attacks. It is widely used in terrorism research. Collection stopped after 2020, events for 1993 are missing, and the project documents collection breaks in 1998, 2008 and 2012, so raw trends need care.

The Ethnic Power Relations Core Dataset codes all politically relevant ethnic groups and their access to state power (from monopoly to discrimination) in all countries from 1946 to 2021. Linked datasets connect groups to armed conflicts (ACD2EPR), territory (GeoEPR), kin abroad and refugees. It is often used in research on ethnic exclusion and civil war, and its expert coding of group relevance is periodically revised.

choosing: Choose the unit before the dataset: conflict-years (UCDP/PRIO, COW, PITF), events (GED, ACLED, event data), actors (NSA, FORGE, UCDP Actor) or agreements (UCDP PA, PA-X). Death thresholds and inclusion rules drive many findings, so test robustness with an alternative list or event source.

Prefer hand-coded sources (GED, ACLED) for counts of violence and use machine-coded event data (GDELT, POLECAT) for broad, timely measures of interaction, validating them against hand-coded data. Merge through UCDP conflict, dyad and actor identifiers and COW or Gleditsch-Ward country codes.
gaps: Many specialised datasets on armed groups, mediation, coups and terrorism end between 2004 and 2017, and the Global Terrorism Database stops at 2020; recent years are covered mainly by UCDP and ACLED.

Non-fatal coercion, sexual violence (covered under HR) and the internal organization of armed groups are thinly documented outside a few regions, and casualty estimates for the most intense recent wars remain uncertain.
Access is becoming more restrictive (ACLED licence, GTD registration, BAAD2 not downloadable), and several project websites have lapsed or been taken over by unrelated content.
